It uses a two-pointer approach (implemented via `pop(0)`) to compare the heads of both lists and append the smaller element to the result list `c`. After one list is exhausted, it appends the remaining elements of the other list. Finally, it prints the result of merging `[1, 3, 5]` and `[2, 4, 6]`.

The logical flow is correct for merging two sorted arrays. The output will be `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]`.
